content: The University of Edinburgh, located in the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland, has collaborated with external experts and WHO staff in the preparation of recommendations. Among the contributors: Dr. Hoang Thi Tran, a neonatologist and Deputy Director of Da Nang Hospital for Women and Children in Vietnam, also serves as the Acting Head of the Department of Paediatrics at the School of Medicine and Pharmacy, University of Da Nang. Professor Khalid Yunis, a specialist in paediatrics and Head of the Division of Neonatology at the Department of Paediatrics and Adolescent Medicine, American University of Beirut Medical Center, Lebanon. Partner organizations and observers include: Deborah Armbruster, Senior Maternal and Newborn Health Advisor at USAID’s Bureau for Global Health, United States. Hilary Gammill, Deputy Director of Maternal, Newborn, and Child Health Discovery and Tools at the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, United States. Leah Greenspan, affiliated with USAID’s Bureau for Global Health in Washington, United States. Dr. William Keenan, Executive Director of the International Pediatric Association, United States. Professor Andrew Shennan, Chair of the FIGO Committee and Professor of Obstetrics at King’s College London, United Kingdom. Dr. Ingela Wiklund, Associate Professor and Board Member at the Karolinska Institute, Sweden, and Head of the Institution for Health and Welfare. The Evidence Synthesis Group (ESG) includes: Jenny Cao, Research Officer in the Maternal, Child, and Adolescent Health Program at the Burnet Institute, Australia. Leanne Jones, Deputy Managing Editor of Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth, University of Liverpool, United Kingdom. Frances Kellie, Managing Editor of Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth, University of Liverpool, United Kingdom. Victoria Hodgetts-Morton, Research Fellow at the University of Birmingham, United Kingdom. Katie Morris, Director of the Birmingham Clinical Trials Unit, University of Birmingham, United Kingdom. Jen Ramson, a guideline methodologist in the Maternal, Child, and Adolescent Health Program at the Burnet Institute, Australia. Dr. Joshua Vogel, Co-Head of the Global Women’s and Newborn’s Health Group at the Burnet Institute, Australia. Myfanwy Williams, Research Associate and guideline methodologist at Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth, University of Liverpool, United Kingdom. The WHO Steering Group includes: Dr. Olufemi Oladapo, Unit Head of the Maternal and Perinatal Health Unit. Dr. Doris Chou, Medical Officer in Maternal and Perinatal Health. Tina Lavin, Technical Officer in Maternal and Perinatal Health. Dr. Maurice Bucagu, Medical Officer in the Maternal Health Unit. Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Unit Head of the Newborn Health Unit. Dr. Ayesha De Costa, Scientist in the Newborn Health Unit. Dr. Karen Edmond, Scientist in the Newborn Health Unit. The External Review Group includes: Dr. Edgardo Abalos, Head of the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology and Vice Director of Centro Rosarino de Estudios Perinatales, Rosario, Argentina. Dr. Philippa Middleton, Associate Professor of Perinatal Epidemiology at the South Australian Health and Medical Research Institute, Adelaide, Australia. Dr. Suneeta Mittal, Professor of Obstetrics and Gynaecology at Fortis Memorial Research Institute, Gurugram, India. Dr. Siddarth Ramji, Professor of Neonatology at Maulana Azad Medical College, New Delhi, India. Dr. Haroon Saloojee, Professor of Paediatrics in the Division of Community Paediatrics at the University of the Witwatersrand, Johannesburg, South Africa. The WHO recommendation on tocolytic therapy for improving preterm birth outcomes was developed with systematic review team leaders, including: Dr. Meghan Bohren, Associate Professor of Gender and Women’s Health at the Centre for Health Equity, University of Melbourne, Australia. Dr. Ioannis Gallos, Clinician and Scientist at Tommy’s National Centre for Miscarriage Research, University of Birmingham, United Kingdom. WHO country and regional offices contributed through: Bremen De Mucio, Advisor in Sexual and Reproductive Health. Adrian Pablo Duran, Advisor in Perinatal Health. Karima Gholbzouri, Regional Advisor. Chandani Anoma Jayathilaka, Medical Officer. Oleg Kuzmenko, Technical Officer in Reproductive Health. Nancy Kidula, Medical Officer in Reproductive, Maternal, and Newborn Health. Priya Mannava, Technical Officer in Health Information. Neena Raina, Coordinator. Howard Sobel, Regional Advisor. Priority outcomes used in decision-making include maternal outcomes (e.g., chorioamnionitis, puerperal sepsis, postnatal fever), adverse effects of treatment, maternal well-being, and maternal satisfaction. Neonatal outcomes include conditions such as cerebral palsy, developmental delay, and sensory impairments (e.g., intellectual, hearing, or visual impairments).
